title: Calculus with Parametric and Polar Curves

questions.q: For the curve $x = t^2$, $y = t^3$, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{3t^2}{2t} = \frac{3t}{2}$ (for $t \neq 0$).

questions.q: Find the arc length of the curve $x = 3t^2$, $y = 2t^3$ for $0 \leq t \leq 2$.
Find the area enclosed by one loop of the rose $r = 3\sin 2\theta$ (for $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi/2$).
questions.answer: $A = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} 9\sin^2 2\theta\,d\theta = \frac{9}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{1-\cos 4\theta}{2}\,d\theta = \frac{9}{4}\left[\theta - \frac{\sin 4\theta}{4}\right]_0^{\pi/2} = \frac{9\pi}{8}$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by the cardioid $r = 2 + 2\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: $A = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} (2+2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi}(4 + 8\cos\theta + 4\cos^2\theta)\,d\theta$. The $\cos\theta$ term integrates to $0$ over a full period, and $\int_0^{2\pi}4\cos^2\theta\,d\theta = 4\pi$: $A = \frac{1}{2}(8\pi + 4\pi) = 6\pi$.

sections.heading: Second derivatives and concavity for parametric curves

questions.q: For $x=t^2$, $y=t^3-3t$, find $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ in terms of $t$, using $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \left[\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\right] \div \frac{dx}{dt}$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3t^2-3}{2t}$. Differentiating with respect to $t$: $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{3t^2-3}{2t}\right) = \frac{(6t)(2t)-(3t^2-3)(2)}{4t^2} = \frac{12t^2-6t^2+6}{4t^2}=\frac{6t^2+6}{4t^2}$. Dividing by $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t$: $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\frac{6t^2+6}{8t^3}=\frac{3(t^2+1)}{4t^3}$.

questions.q: Find the area inside the circle $r=3$ and outside the circle $r=2$ (an annular region).

sections.heading: Horizontal and vertical tangents on parametric curves

questions.q: For $x=t^2-4$, $y=t^3-3t$, find the value(s) of $t$ where the tangent line is horizontal ($\frac{dy}{dt}=0$, $\frac{dx}{dt}\neq0$).
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dt}=3t^2-3=0$ gives $t=\pm1$. Check $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t\neq0$ at both: valid. Horizontal tangents at $t=1$ and $t=-1$.

questions.q: For the same curve, find the value(s) of $t$ where the tangent line is vertical ($\frac{dx}{dt}=0$, $\frac{dy}{dt}\neq0$).
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t=0$ gives $t=0$. Check $\frac{dy}{dt}=3(0)^2-3=-3\neq0$: valid. Vertical tangent at $t=0$.

sections.heading: Converting between polar and Cartesian for calculus

questions.q: Find the slope of the tangent line to $r=1+\sin\theta$ at $\theta=0$, using $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$ as parametric equations in $\theta$.
questions.answer: $x=(1+\sin\theta)\cos\theta$, $y=(1+\sin\theta)\sin\theta$. $\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\cos\theta\cos\theta-(1+\sin\theta)\sin\theta = \cos^2\theta-\sin\theta-\sin^2\theta$; at $\theta=0$: $1-0-0=1$. $\frac{dy}{d\theta}=\cos\theta\sin\theta+(1+\sin\theta)\cos\theta$; at $\theta=0$: $0+1=1$. Slope $=\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}=\frac{1}{1}=1$.

sections.heading: Speed and length for parametric motion

questions.q: A particle moves according to $x(t)=t^2$, $y(t)=4t$. Find its speed at $t=3$.
Find the arc length of $x=\cos^3t$, $y=\sin^3t$ for $0\leq t\leq\frac{\pi}{2}$ (an astroid arc), using $\frac{dx}{dt}=-3\cos^2t\sin t$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}=3\sin^2t\cos t$.
questions.answer: $\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)^2 = 9\cos^4t\sin^2t+9\sin^4t\cos^2t = 9\sin^2t\cos^2t(\cos^2t+\sin^2t)=9\sin^2t\cos^2t$. So the speed is $3|\sin t\cos t|$. $L=\int_0^{\pi/2}3\sin t\cos t\,dt = \left[\frac{3}{2}\sin^2t\right]_0^{\pi/2}=\frac{3}{2}$.

sections.heading: Slope and concavity for polar-derived curves

questions.q: Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for the polar curve $r=2\theta$ at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$, using $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$.
questions.answer: $x=2\theta\cos\theta$, $y=2\theta\sin\theta$. $\frac{dx}{d\theta}=2\cos\theta-2\theta\sin\theta$; at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$: $0-\pi=-\pi$. $\frac{dy}{d\theta}=2\sin\theta+2\theta\cos\theta$; at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$: $2+0=2$. Slope $=\frac{2}{-\pi}=-\frac{2}{\pi}$.

questions.q: For $x=t^3-3t$, $y=t^2$, find the points where the tangent is horizontal.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dt}=2t=0$ gives $t=0$. Check $\frac{dx}{dt}=3t^2-3=-3\neq0$ at $t=0$: valid. Horizontal tangent at $t=0$, i.e. the point $(x,y)=(0,0)$.

sections.heading: Arc length of a polar curve

questions.q: Set up (do not evaluate) the arc length integral for the circle $r=4$ over $0\leq\theta\leq2\pi$, using $L=\int_\alpha^\beta\sqrt{r^2+\left(\frac{dr}{d\theta}\right)^2}\,d\theta$, and verify the setup is consistent with the known circumference formula.
questions.answer: $\frac{dr}{d\theta}=0$: $L=\int_0^{2\pi}\sqrt{16+0}\,d\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}4\,d\theta=8\pi$, matching the circumference $2\pi r=2\pi(4)=8\pi$ of a circle with radius $4$.

questions.q: A projectile's position is given by $x(t)=20t$, $y(t)=15t-4.9t^2$ (meters, seconds). Find the projectile's velocity components $\frac{dx}{dt}$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}$, and find the speed at $t=1$.
For the same projectile, find the time at which the vertical velocity is $0$ (the peak of the trajectory).
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dt}=15-9.8t=0$ gives $t=\frac{15}{9.8}\approx1.53$ s.

questions.q: The cardioid $r=1+\cos\theta$ is symmetric about the polar axis. Use this symmetry to explain why the total area enclosed can be computed as $2\times$ the area for $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$, and evaluate the total area.
questions.answer: Since $r(\theta)=r(-\theta)$, the curve is symmetric about the polar axis, so the area for $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ equals the area for $\theta\in[-\pi,0]$. Total area $=2\cdot\frac{1}{2}\int_0^\pi(1+\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta=\int_0^\pi\left(1+2\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta\right)d\theta=\left[\theta+2\sin\theta+\frac{\theta}{2}+\frac{\sin2\theta}{4}\right]_0^\pi=\pi+0+\frac{\pi}{2}+0=\frac{3\pi}{2}$.

questions.q: For the parametric curve $x=e^t\cos t$, $y=e^t\sin t$, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $t=0$, using $\frac{dx}{dt}=e^t(\cos t-\sin t)$ and $\frac{dy}{dt}=e^t(\sin t+\cos t)$.
questions.answer: At $t=0$: $\frac{dx}{dt}=e^0(1-0)=1$. $\frac{dy}{dt}=e^0(0+1)=1$. Slope $=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}=\frac{1}{1}=1$.

questions.q: A Ferris wheel of radius 10 m, centered 12 m above the ground, rotates so that a rider's position is $x(t)=10\cos t$, $y(t)=12+10\sin t$, where $t$ is measured in radians and represents elapsed angle since the rider was at the rightmost point. Find the rider's height above the ground when $t=\frac{\pi}{3}$, and find the vertical velocity $\frac{dy}{dt}$ at that instant (assuming $t$ increases at a constant rate of $1$ rad per unit time).
questions.answer: Height: $y\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=12+10\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=12+10\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=12+5\sqrt{3}\approx20.66$ m. Vertical velocity: $\frac{dy}{dt}=10\cos t$; at $t=\frac{\pi}{3}$: $10\cdot\frac{1}{2}=5$ (units of height per unit time).

sections.heading: Total distance traveled along a parametric path

questions.q: A robot on a factory floor follows the path $x(t)=t^2$, $y(t)=2t$ for $0\leq t\leq3$ (meters, seconds). Set up the arc length integral for the total distance traveled, and evaluate it exactly using the substitution $u=t^2+1$ where appropriate.
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=2$: $L=\int_0^3\sqrt{4t^2+4}\,dt=2\int_0^3\sqrt{t^2+1}\,dt$. This does not simplify via a simple power-rule substitution (it requires a trigonometric or hyperbolic substitution to evaluate in closed form), but can be set up as $L=2\int_0^3\sqrt{t^2+1}\,dt$, which numerically evaluates to approximately $2(5.20)=10.40$ m.
